guide_cc_channel_p_errorloop: When the bridge fails to deliver a reply to the EClaw API (expired API Key, network error, quota exceeded, etc.), notifyClaudeError injects the error into Claude's channel inbox so Claude knows the previous reply did not reach the user and can retry or adjust. The user also sees a bridge error hint on the next message.
guide_cc_channel_p_faq_context: A classic symptom of context pressure — Claude “forgets” the fakechat instructions. The Context Pressure Monitor (20% warning / 5% auto /clear) and Reply Tool Enforcer should handle this automatically. You can also manually send Escape + /clear in the tmux pane to reset context immediately.

guide_cc_channel_p_faq_log: The bridge log is at /tmp/eclaw-bridge.log; the PreToolUse hook log is at /tmp/eclaw-hook.log.
guide_cc_channel_p_faq_reply_fail: Usual causes: expired ECLAW_API_KEY, claude.ai weekly quota exhausted, or a transient 5xx from the EClaw API. The Error Feedback Loop pushes the error into Claude's inbox and the user also sees a bridge hint. Rotate the API key or wait for the quota reset to recover.
guide_cc_channel_p_kanban_queue: By default the bridge treats automated messages from EClaw's kanban board as Claude's work queue and forwards them (ECLAW_FORWARD_KANBAN=true). If the bot hits a context overflow and you need emergency mute, temporarily set it to false to stop forwarding kanban messages without affecting user-initiated messages.

guide_hermes_channel_note_entity_id: If the entity_id you pick is taken, EClawbot returns Entity already bound. Pick an empty slot — do NOT use DELETE /api/device/entity/:id/permanent (irreversible; wipes the entity's chat history and XP).
guide_hermes_channel_p_faq_auth: EClaw pushes webhooks with Authorization: Bearer <callback_token>, but Hermes's built-in webhook gateway expects HMAC-SHA256 signatures. The two schemes are incompatible. The bridge intercepts before the gateway, validates the Bearer token itself, then forwards — so the gateway-level HMAC must be skipped. For production, add a reverse proxy that supports both.
guide_hermes_channel_p_faq_cold: Since 2026-04-28 the bridge talks to hermes_daemon.py (option B) — the daemon boots a single persistent hermes --continue child, so cold-start cost is paid once. Per-message latency ≈ Hermes inference time (typically 1–3s). When HERMES_DAEMON_URL is unset or the daemon is unreachable, the bridge falls back to the legacy per-request hermes chat subprocess; that path still shows the old 7–9s cold start. Background + fallback semantics: KNOW-HOW §14, SPEC-bridge-refactor.md.
guide_hermes_channel_p_faq_multiple: Yes, fully isolated. Each channel uses its own eck_... key and binds a different entity slot — no conflicts. To serve multiple entities from one Hermes container, bind multiple times (each entity gets its own botSecret). The current bridge handles a single entity; multi-entity support requires reading multiple HERMES_ECLAW_ENTITY_ID values and dispatching inside process_message.
guide_hermes_channel_p_faq_provider: Hermes v1 changed the config schema. The old provider: minimax at the top level is silently ignored — use model: { provider: minimax, name: MiniMax-M2.7 }. Run hermes doctor to confirm — it will explicitly warn about "Stale root-level config keys". Fix and restart the bridge.
guide_hermes_channel_p_faq_zombie: Docker containers where PID 1 isn't a proper init (e.g. openclaw-b uses openclaw as PID 1) don't reap children, so asyncio.create_subprocess_exec's communicate() can hang forever when the subprocess exits abnormally. The bridge wraps it in asyncio.wait_for with a 90s timeout — if you see timed out after 90s, it usually means the LLM API is down (check minimax status).

guide_hermes_channel_p_what1: Hermes Channel is a Python bridge (aiohttp) that lets Hermes Agent (NousResearch's self-improving AI agent) bind to an EClawbot entity as a native bot — alongside OpenClaw Channel / Claude Code Channel.
guide_hermes_channel_p_what2: On inbound message, the bridge invokes the Hermes CLI to get a reply, then POSTs it back to EClawbot. All Hermes features (tools, skills, memory, sessions) are available. A KNOW-HOW doc in the repo records 15 pitfalls hit during development — copy-paste ready.

guide_hermes_channel_warning_quick_tunne: ⚠️ Do NOT use Quick Tunnel (--url ...) inside the container: the container's UDP buffer is too small for QUIC, causing constant disconnects. Always use a named tunnel (--token ...) — stable and gives you a fixed domain.
guide_hermes_channel_warning_teardown: ⚠️ Teardown uses safe unbind (DELETE /api/entity, requires botSecret) — it does NOT touch entity data. To wipe the entity slot entirely, use DELETE /api/device/entity/:id/permanent (irreversible — think twice).
guide_pub_meta: 10 content platforms · multi-tenant keys live for all (Telegraph is auto-key, no vault needed)
guide_pub_overview_desc: backend/article-publisher.js unifies 10 content platforms under /api/publisher/<platform>/*. "Multi-tenant" means each device uses keys from its own vault when calling the platform — instead of every device sharing the owner's single env key. All 9 key-requiring platforms (X, Hashnode, DEV.to, Qiita, LinkedIn, Reddit, Tumblr, Blogger, WeChat) run the full vault-first flow: each platform has its own resolve<Platform>Creds(deviceId) that reads the device vault first and falls back to process.env on miss. Telegraph is auto-key (first call auto-creates an anonymous account) so it doesn't need a vault path.
guide_pub_roadmap_desc: Completed 2026-04. All 9 key-requiring platforms run vault-first; Telegraph is auto-key and doesn't need a vault path. Always backwards-compat: missing vault keys fall back to process.env, so existing env-only deployments are unaffected. The list below groups platforms by signing pattern with the shipping PR for each:
guide_pub_roadmap_h: Done: multi-tenant migration shipped on every platform ✅
guide_pub_roadmap_step1: 1-key bearer platforms (Hashnode / DEV.to / Qiita): a single API token — the simplest, shipped first.
guide_pub_roadmap_step2: 2-key bearer + URN (LinkedIn): access_token + author URN, both pulled from the vault.
guide_pub_roadmap_step3: 4-key OAuth1a real-time signing (X / Tumblr): consumer + access pairs, every request signs nonce + timestamp with HMAC-SHA1.
guide_pub_roadmap_step4: 4-key OAuth2 password grant + per-tenant token cache (Reddit): username/password trades for an access_token; cache keyed by Map keyed by clientId+username to prevent cross-tenant pollution.
guide_pub_roadmap_step5: OAuth2 authorization-code / app-credential + per-tenant token cache (Blogger / WeChat): Blogger goes through a user consent flow for refresh_token (stored per-device in DB); WeChat uses AppID/AppSecret to mint ~2h access_tokens, cached by Map keyed by appId.

guide_usecase_faq_rotate:
Q: What if my Device Secret leaks, or I want to rotate it periodically?
A: Settings → press the 🔄 Rotate button next to the Device Secret row. The old secret is invalidated immediately — any API call using it will return 403, so you must update the new secret on your phone app, Channel plugin, vault, and anywhere else it's stored. The new secret is shown only once — press "Download .txt backup" to save a copy.

guide_vm_pain: Three pain points before Vector Memory
guide_vm_pain1: ❌ Forgets everything once the context window is full — yesterday's conversation has to be retold today
guide_vm_pain2: ❌ Multiple bots, no unified view — owners can't browse conversations across bots from one place
guide_vm_pain3: ❌ Answers with no receipts — you can't ask "where does that come from?"
guide_vm_sp1_desc: Every message is written into pgvector. Even a month later, in a different session, on a different device — if the meaning is close, it can be retrieved and cited. Memory lives at the database layer, not the prompt layer — no more hostage to 8k / 32k / 200k token limits.
